intro: A Modbus device keeps its values in registers: numbered 16-bit boxes. Every device has its own register map, the list of which register holds what, so every new device means a new manual. SunSpec fixes the map. A device lays out its data in numbered models: blocks of registers, each with a known order of values. A controller finds the models by itself, one after the other, and reads any SunSpec inverter, battery or meter the same way.
plain: SunSpec is one shared layout for the readings inside solar power converters, batteries and meters. Without it, each maker lists them in its own order, so every new device needs its own manual. With SunSpec, every device fills in the same form, in the same order, with a label at the top of each page. So one program can read devices from any maker the same way.

find.title: Find the SunSpec marker
find.text: The plant controller knows nothing about this inverter yet. It reads two registers at address 40000, the usual place to look. They hold the letters "SunS": this device follows SunSpec, and its map can be found instead of typed in.

common.title: Who are you?
common.text: The first model is always the common model, ID 1: who made the device, what it is, its serial number. Every model starts with a header of two registers: its ID, which says what kind of model it is, and its length in registers.

walk.title: Find the next model
walk.text: The controller skips over the common model by its length: 40002 + 2 + 66 = 40070. There it finds model 103, a three-phase inverter (one that feeds all three live wires of the grid), 50 registers long.

read.title: Read power and frequency
read.text: Registers hold only whole numbers of 16 bits. So each value comes with a scale factor in another register: the power of ten to multiply it by. W (active power) = 4820 with W_SF = 0 is 4820 × 1 = 4820 W. Hz (grid frequency) = 5001 with Hz_SF = −2 is 5001 × 0.01 = 50.01 Hz.

end.title: End of the list
end.text: The controller jumps again, to 40070 + 2 + 50 = 40122, and finds ID 0xFFFF: no more models. It now knows every model the inverter has and where each value lives.

frames.values-req: Send me W, W_SF, Hz and Hz_SF

tid-1.name: Transaction ID 1
tid-1.note: A number the controller picks. The answer carries the same one, so the controller can match them.

tid-2.name: Transaction ID 2
tid-2.note: The next request, the next number.

proto.name: Protocol ID
proto.note: 0x0000: Modbus. SunSpec adds no bytes of its own: it is plain Modbus TCP.

len-6.name: Length
len-6.note: 6 bytes follow: the unit ID and 5 bytes of request.

fc03.name: Function 03
fc03.note: 0x03: read holding registers. SunSpec data lives there.

addr-40000.name: Address 40000
addr-40000.note: 0x9C40 = 40000: where SunSpec looks first. If the marker is not there, a client tries 0, then 50000.

addr-40002.name: Address 40002
addr-40002.note: 0x9C42: right after the marker, the first model's header.

addr-40084.name: Address 40084
addr-40084.note: 0x9C94: W. The model's data starts at 40072, and W is always its 13th register.

qty-4.name: Count
qty-4.note: 4 registers: W, W_SF, Hz and Hz_SF, one after the other.

qty-68.name: Count
qty-68.note: 0x0044 = 68 registers: the header (2) and the common model (66), in one read.

suns.name: SunSpec ID
suns.note: 0x53756E53: "SunS" in ASCII. Models start right after it.

id-1.name: ID 1
id-1.note: The common model. Every SunSpec device has it first.

l-66.name: L 66
l-66.note: 0x0042 = 66: the registers that follow this header, up to the next model.

mn.name: Mn
mn.note: Manufacturer: "Example". A string always takes all its registers, 16 here, two characters in each. Zeros fill the rest.

opt.name: Opt
opt.note: Options, 8 registers: all zeros, which means not used.

vr.name: Vr
vr.note: Version, 8 registers: firmware (the device's own software) "3.4.1".

da.name: DA
da.note: Device address: the unit ID it answers to, 1.

pad.name: Pad
pad.note: One filler register that makes the length even. Its value means nothing.

id-103.name: ID 103
id-103.note: 0x0067 = 103: a three-phase inverter, with integers and scale factors.

w.name: W
w.note: 0x12D4 = 4820: AC power, before scaling. W is signed: it can be negative.

w-sf.name: W_SF
w-sf.note: 0: multiply W by 10⁰ = 1. Power is 4820 W.

hz-sf.name: Hz_SF
hz-sf.note: 0xFFFE, read as a signed number, is −2: multiply Hz by 10⁻² = 0.01. Frequency is 50.01 Hz.

id-end.name: ID 0xFFFF
id-end.note: The end model: no more models follow.

l-0.name: L 0
l-0.note: The end model has no data.

a-at.name: Header
a-at.note: The model's first register: its ID.

a-id.name: ID
a-id.note: 103: which model this is. The number says what every register in it means.

a-l.name: L
a-l.note: 50: how many registers follow the header.

a-body.name: Data
a-body.note: The model's values, in a fixed order. W is always 12 registers in.

a-next.name: Next header
a-next.note: Where the next model starts: header + 2 + L.

a-raw.name: Hz
a-raw.note: The register as sent: a whole number.

a-sf.name: Hz_SF
a-sf.note: The scale factor: a power of ten, from −10 to 10. One scale factor can serve several values.

a-real.name: Value
a-real.note: What it means: 5001 × 10⁻² = 50.01 Hz. A 16-bit register cannot hold 50.01, but this way it can.

facts.standard: SunSpec Modbus, by the SunSpec Alliance. IEEE 1547-2018 names it as one of three protocols a grid-connected inverter may offer.
facts.between: Controller or logger → inverter, battery, meter
facts.model: Numbered models: 1 common, 101 to 103 inverters, 201 to 204 meters, the 700 series for newer inverters
facts.frames: Plain Modbus: reads with FC 03, writes with FC 06 and FC 16

tips: Do not copy register numbers from one device to another. Walk the models from the base address, where "SunS" is: the same model can sit somewhere else on the next device.
Some devices give the common model a length of 65, without the pad. Always jump by the length the device sends.
0x8000 in a signed register or a scale factor, and 0xFFFF in an unsigned one, mean "not implemented". Do not show them as −32768 or 65535.
Read a value and its scale factor in one request. Two separate reads can pair a new value with an old scale factor.

anatomy.header: A model header, and how a client jumps to the next one
anatomy.scale: A value and its scale factor

playground.file: The inverter's SunSpec models, as a controller would note them after the walk. On a real device, the walk finds them; nobody types them in.
playground.unit: The Modbus unit ID. SunSpec works the same over TCP and over RS-485.
playground.base: The base address: where the marker "SunS" is. SunSpec allows 40000, 0 and 50000.
playground.common: Model 1 is always first. Its header is right after the marker.
playground.model: Model 103: a three-phase inverter. 101 is single-phase, 102 split-phase.
playground.length: The length tells where the next model starts: 40070 + 2 + 50 = 40122.
playground.w: W: 12 registers into the model's data. Its scale factor is the next register.
playground.sf: A scale factor is a signed power of ten. It may be different on each device.
playground.acc: An accumulator: total energy in two registers, high word first. It only counts up.
playground.end: ID 65535 (0xFFFF), length 0: the end of the list.
